raw_response:
I've been working this land since I was 14. My father taught me, and his father taught him. Quzhou's soil and water — I know them in my bones. Forty-five years tells me more than any book could.

My wheat-maize rotation on most of the land is not changing. That's my foundation. Reliable income, I know what to do, and the county supply station always has what I need. I'll put 14 mu into that rotation. For the remaining 4 mu, I'll keep cotton. My children say to drop it — too much work, they're right about the labor — but I've grown cotton my whole life and I still get decent prices if the season is good. Four mu I can manage mostly by myself and my wife.

For wheat, I'll do three waterings from the well: once before winter sets in to help the roots, once at jointing, once at heading. I'll put down compound fertilizer as base and top-dress urea at jointing. Same as always. Rotary till after the maize comes off in September, then sow in early October.

For summer maize, I'll direct-seed right after wheat harvest in June — no tilling, saves time and the soil stays moist. Hybrid seed from the township shop. I'll apply fertilizer once as base and top-dress around jointing. Two waterings unless rain is good.

Cotton gets the deepest attention. I'll plough that plot in spring, apply more potash because cotton needs it, and water four times through the season. Pest pressure is the real worry — bollworm and aphids — so I'll spray five or six times. My wife handles most of the topping and picking.
